title: Smoothness, separatedness and properness of the degree components

proof.text: (1) First the hypotheses of the cited nodes. $C$ is nonempty (it has the point $P$), connected, separated, of finite type, of dimension one and smooth over the algebraically closed field $k$, so it is a Noetherian integral scheme by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] (1), hence a curve in the sense of [def-pc-curve]; it is proper of dimension $1$ over $k$, hence projective over $k$ by [lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective]. Thus $C$ is a smooth projective curve over $k$ with the $k$-rational point $P$, and since $k$ is algebraically closed it is separably closed, so [prop-pc-xk-integral] (2) shows that every base change $C_K$ ($K/k$ a field extension) is a smooth projective curve; in particular $C$ is geometrically integral, hence geometrically irreducible and geometrically connected. These are the hypotheses of [thm-pc-picard-representable], [det-picard-f-representable-chart], [lem-pc-twist], [thm-pc-hilb-curves], [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism], [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-surjective] and [lem-sc-hilb-geometrically-integral] used below. Now [thm-pc-picard-representable] supplies the representing group scheme and its multiplication and inverse. Let $W\subset H_g$ be the chart of [det-picard-f-representable-chart]; by its clause (1), $h_W\cong F\subset\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k,P}\cong\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$, and by [lem-pc-f-open-subfunctor] the inclusion $F\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k,P}$ is representable by open immersions, so $W\to\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ is an open immersion; the chart node (2) says that $W$ is smooth of pure dimension $g$, and $W$ is of finite type over $k$, being open in the variety $H_g$ ([thm-pc-hilb-curves]). For any $k$-point $M$ of the group scheme, translation by $M$ is an isomorphism, so $M^{-1}W$ is an open subscheme isomorphic to $W$. If $t$ is a point with residue field $K$ and corresponding rigidified line bundle $\mathcal L_t$ on $C_K$, [lem-pc-twist] gives a line bundle $\mathcal M_0$ on $C$ with $h^0(C_K,\mathcal L_t\otimes\mathcal M_{0,K})=1$ and $H^1(C_K,\mathcal L_t\otimes\mathcal M_{0,K})=0$; since $C_K$ is a smooth projective curve over $K$, $H^i(C_K,-)=0$ for $i\ge2$ by [lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim], so $Rf_{K,*}(\mathcal L_t\otimes\mathcal M_{0,K})=R\Gamma(C_K,\mathcal L_t\otimes\mathcal M_{0,K})$ is a complex of $K$-vector spaces with cohomology $K$ in degree $0$ only, hence isomorphic to $K[0]$, i.e. the class of $\mathcal L_t\otimes\mathcal M_{0,K}$ (rigidified along $P$) lies in $F(K)$. Hence $M\cdot t\in W$, i.e. $t$ lies in the translate $M^{-1}W$ for $M=[\mathcal M_0]$. These translates cover the Picard scheme, proving it is locally of finite type and smooth of pure dimension $g$. Finally, [lem-sc-group-scheme-separated-field] says that every group scheme over a field is separated, so $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ is separated.

proof.text: (2) By (1), $C$ satisfies the hypotheses of the nodes cited here (separably closed $k$, smooth projective geometrically integral curve of genus $g$). The universal effective divisor on $C\times H_g$ and its associated line bundle give the morphism $\alpha$ by [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]; normalization along $P$ changes the line bundle only by pullback from $H_g$, hence gives the same class in the Picard functor. For an algebraically closed extension $K/k$ and a degree-$g$ line bundle $\mathcal L$ on $C_K$, [lem-sc-riemann-roch] gives $\chi(\mathcal L)=1$, so $\mathcal L$ has a nonzero section. Its zero divisor is an effective Cartier divisor of degree $g$, and [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism] sends the corresponding $K$-point of $H_g$ to $[\mathcal L]$. Equivalently, the surjectivity statement is [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-surjective] specialized to $d=g$. Thus $\alpha$ is surjective.

proof.text: (3) By (2), $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ is the surjective image of the proper scheme $H_g$ (properness and smoothness are in [thm-pc-hilb-curves], applicable because $C$ is geometrically irreducible by (1)). Its structure morphism is separated and locally of finite type by (1); therefore [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] makes $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ proper. For every field extension $K/k$, the base change $H_{g,K}$ is integral by [lem-sc-hilb-geometrically-integral], and the base-changed Abel map is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The image of this irreducible space is irreducible by [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-continuous-image], so $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ is geometrically irreducible. Smoothness and pure dimension $g$ follow from (1), hence the degree-$g$ component is a smooth proper geometrically irreducible variety and therefore geometrically connected. Finally, [det-picard-main-degree] (3) identifies tensoring by $\mathcal O_C((d-g)P)$ with an isomorphism $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^d_{C/k}$, transferring all these properties to every $d$.
